summary: Configurable burst-gap behavior and rate-shedding guidance for dedicated pool causing unexpected 429s
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429 responses from a dedicated pool after enabling a short 'burst-gap' window in their tenant rate configuration. The 429s appear non-uniform across keys and persist after removing transient warmup traffic.
Impact: StreamlineAI ingestion pipeline experiences ~8-12% failed requests for short bursts, leading to delayed embeddings and backoff storms in their orchestrator. Affects production latency SLAs for several endpoints.
Environment: Dedicated pool in us-west, tenant StreamlineAI, models pinned to redwood-open-3B. Config change applied via Console -> Rate Limits on 2026-03-09 at 03:45 UTC.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure tenant burst-gap = 5s and burst-pool-refill = 30s for dedicated pool.
2) Start 80 parallel workers issuing 4 concurrent streaming sessions each (320 concurrent streams) with mostly short-lived sessions (~6s).
3) Observe 429 rate increase after ~90s and persistent soft-throttle even when traffic subsides.
Expected behavior: Temporary increase in short-window rejects but smooth refill after gap ends; no sticky 429s affecting steady-state low-volume traffic.
Actual behavior: 429s continue for minutes after traffic drop, and some API keys report asymmetric throttle headers.
Key traces/logs: edge-request-id=edg-9a4f2, tenant_request_id=stl-20260309-001, sample throttle headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining:0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 25s, but other connections show Remaining>0. Console shows burst-pool-credit dropped to 0 and recovered slowly.
Immediate ask: Investigation into burst-gap semantics in dedicated pools, guidance for configuration to avoid sticky post-burst throttling, and recommended warmup/worker patterns.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged; collecting tenant config and recent audit logs. Asked customer for exporter traces and worker concurrency patterns.

2026-03-10 11:03 - StreamlineAI (Customer): Provided sample orchestrator logs and stated they enabled burst-gap to allow short spikes from mobile clients. Noted that the issue began after update to their orchestrator on 2026-03-09 03:30 UTC.

2026-03-10 14:27 - Marco Chen (SRE): Reproduced similar pattern in isolated dedicated dev pool with synthetics; hypothesis: burst-gap combined with refill interval can cause token accounting misalignment across HTTP/2 connection reuse.
2026-03-11 08:50 - Marco Chen (SRE): Requested customer to temporarily revert burst-gap to 0 and monitor. Also suggested enabling per-route isolation for interactive streams as a workaround.

2026-03-11 12:20 - StreamlineAI (Customer): Reverted burst-gap; observed immediate reduction in 429 rate but still saw occasional sticky 429s on long-lived gRPC connections. Provided additional traces (edge-request-id=edg-9a4f2-B).
investigation_notes: Initial reproduction used 320 concurrent short streams; saw 'token window' exhaustion in the dedicated-rate-limiter pod log (rate-limiter@pod-7c): 'refill-mismatch: window-start 1618033 vs expected 1618030'.
Observed HTTP/2 connection reuse caused per-connection token deltas to be applied twice when an edge proxy reweighted a connection (NAT pool reuse).
Burst-pool accounting is global per-tenant, but burst-gap introduces a temporary per-connection 'hold' which can delay credit redistribution after a drop in traffic.
Found related config edge-case: when burst-gap < avg session TTL and refill interval is coarse, credits can be transiently orphaned on dead connections until keepalive cleanup runs.
Linked to prior bug FIX in PR #348 which addressed double-accounting during ephemeral key rotations; further adjustments needed for dedicated pools with aggressive refill windows.
resolution:
Workaround applied: advised customer to set burst-gap to 0 or to increase burst-gap > average session duration while reducing burst-pool-refill granularity (recommended 60s). Enabled per-route isolation for interactive streams and applied a temporary connection-drain policy on edge proxy to expedite orphaned-credit reclamation. Observed 95% reduction in 429s within 20 minutes after changes.
Permanent fix/next steps: Engineering to schedule a rate-limiter patch to detect and reclaim orphaned per-connection holds earlier (ticketed INT-330221). Action item: update Console UI to show per-connection hold counters and a 'force reclaim' button for dedicated admins. Customer follow-up planned in 2026-03-18 to validate at scale.
resolution_status: Workaround in place; engineering fix scheduled
